BiblicalUsage: Bea is the Aramaic word for seeking and asking. It is the word for Daniel going in to ask the king for time, for Daniel and his companions desiring mercies of the God of heaven over the king's secret, for the men who seek to find occasion against Daniel in the law of his God, and for Daniel coming to one who stands by to ask the truth of the vision.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe seeking in Daniel is always seeking God first, because the king's secret is sought from heaven and not from men. Daniel asks the king for time and asks God for the answer, and I hold that the order matters: ask God, and the king's question answers itself.
